title: Caller identity attestation sequential committed-use replay control
governing_question: After one committed execution has used a valid authenticated caller identity attestation, does the successor execution path natively refuse reuse of that exact same attestation across a separate execution carrying a fresh otherwise-valid permit?
target_property: Sequential committed-use single-use control for authenticated caller identity attestations.
required_preconditions: P4-F03 predecessor evidence identity is preserved.
Both adversarial executions use the same human authority, agent identity, policy context, caller identity issuer, and authenticated subject semantics.
Each adversarial execution receives a fresh distinct otherwise-valid execution permit.
The replayed caller identity attestation remains cryptographically and temporally valid during both uses.
No permit replay is used to obtain the result.
No authority revocation, policy change, identity mismatch, signature tamper, expiry, or unrelated refusal condition is introduced.

positive_control.description: Two separate executions use fresh distinct permits and fresh distinct valid caller identity attestations.

adversarial_case.description: Execution one uses caller attestation X with fresh permit P1 and commits. Execution two then presents the exact same still-valid caller attestation X with a separate fresh permit P2.
identity_requirements: P1 and P2 have distinct permit identities.
The exact same caller attestation identity is used in both adversarial executions.
The replayed attestation remains independently valid during the second execution.

requirements: The first use of attestation X commits.
The second use of the exact same attestation X with fresh permit P2 is refused before consequence.
The refusal is specifically attributable to a native caller-attestation replay or consumed-state control.
The refusal is not caused by permit replay or another unrelated control.
Witness evidence preserves reused attestation identity, distinct permit identities, first committed use, and second replay refusal.
The first use of attestation X commits.
The second use of the same still-valid attestation X with a fresh distinct permit also commits.

non_discriminating_conditions: The replayed caller attestation identity is not identical.
The replayed attestation is expired, tampered, cryptographically invalid, or otherwise independently invalid.
The second execution is refused for an unrelated reason rather than native attestation replay or consumed-state control.
Required predecessor, source, or witness identity cannot be established.
witness_requirements: Preserve caller identity attestation ID for each governed execution.
Preserve permit ID for each governed execution.
Distinguish first committed use from second attempted reuse.
Preserve the native replay-refusal reason when refusal occurs.
successor_boundary: Tests sequential reuse after an earlier committed execution.
Does not establish atomic protection against simultaneous or concurrent replay.
Does not establish network, transport, process, hardware, operating-system, external identity-provider, or credential-compromise resistance.
Does not establish tenant isolation, distributed replay protection, production exploitability resistance, or general swarm security.
execution_rule: Freeze this definition before successor implementation or behavioral execution. Preserve predecessor V08 and P4-F03 evidence unchanged.
